one_month_reasoning: The main scheduled event in the window to 2026-11-08 is Generac's Q3 2026 report. Alpha Vantage's calendar estimates 2026-11-04 (consensus EPS about $2.38-2.43), and the company has reported Q3 between Oct 24 and Nov 6 in every year since 2013. Over the last 20 reports the mean absolute earnings-day move was 8.9% (median 7.7%), with 12 of 20 up days, so a +/-9% jump is likely inside the window. Two things lean negative. Q3 EPS estimates were cut 14 times against 3 raises in the last 30 days. Kalshi prices the 2026 Atlantic season as quiet: P(more than 4 hurricanes) is about 7%, and outages ran below baseline in Q2 per management. That weighs on residential home standby, the part of the business that missed in Q3 2025 (-4.9% on the day, -17% over 10 days). Two things lean positive. The stock has rallied 28% since the Sept 16 pre-Amazon low on the Amazon deal and the KeyBanc and Piper upgrades. And C&I/data-center commentary (backlog, second hyperscaler terms) could dominate the print, as in Q1 2026 (+16.5%). These roughly offset. I used a near-symmetric lognormal with a median of about $223.5, a hair below spot, and a 1-month sigma of about 15.5%: annual vol of 56% / 3.5 = 16%, consistent with the stock's own 21-day log-return sd of 14.3% over the last 3 years plus the earnings event. No index, lock-up or regulatory event that matters is scheduled. The FOMC meets in the window but is not a stock-specific driver.

fair_value.method: Blend of three methods: 2027 consensus EPS $12.67 x 20.5x P/E = $260 (40%); 2027E EBITDA $1.22B x 15x EV/EBITDA less $1.06B net debt over 59.4M shares = $289 (30%); Generac's own 2019-2025 median trailing P/E of 21.5x on estimated horizon trailing EPS of $12.03 = $259 (30%). Weighted result is about $268, roughly 19% above the $224.94 close.

inputs_detail.input: Peer forward P/E, residential/cyclical subset (CMI, ENPH, AOS, LII)
inputs_detail.derivation: Median of the four peers' forward P/E: (14.47+15.94)/2 = 15.2x

inputs_detail.input: Peer forward P/E, data-center electrical subset (HUBB, CAT, POWL, NVT, ETN, VRT)

inputs_detail.derivation: C&I was 47% of Q2 2026 sales ($556.5M of $1,177.8M). C&I is guided to low-30s % growth in 2026, and a $1.35B data-center backlog is scheduled for 2027 delivery, so C&I is roughly half of the mix over the horizon.

The 50/50 blend 0.5x15.2 + 0.5x28.6 = 21.9x, cut about 6% to 20.5x. Reasons for the cut: revenue is concentrated in two hyperscalers, and there are the 2022-23 guidance-cut episodes. 20.5x sits inside the peer range (14.4-79.1x), below the 28.1x peer median, and next to GNRC's own 2019-2025 median year-end trailing P/E of 21.5x (computed from sources 5 and 6). A 2027 EPS base is conservative because at Oct 2027 the market will price 2028 EPS.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 2027E revenue $6.397B x 19.0% margin = EBITDA $1.2155B; x15x = EV $18.23B; less net debt $1.06B = equity $17.17B; / 59.37M shares = $289.2

inputs_detail.derivation: FY2026 guidance is 20.0-21.0% including about 1.5pt from tariff refunds, so 18.5-19.5% underlying. I held the midpoint of 19.0% flat because the lower-margin data-center mix offsets operating leverage.

Peer EV/EBITDA figures are trailing. The residential subset median is 13.7x (12.21, 15.22) and the data-center subset median is 27.0x (26.93, 27.13); a 50/50 blend gives 20.4x trailing. My EBITDA is a forward 2027 figure about 30% above 2026 (consensus revenue 6.397/4.937 = 1.296), so I divided 20.4 by 1.3 to get about 15.7x and rounded down to 15x. That is inside the full peer range of 10.4-197.7x and below the 26.0x median.
Short-term borrowings $48.3M + current portion $32.1M + long-term $1,249.0M - cash $264.9M = $1,064.5M
59.06M shares outstanding + 0.308M Amazon warrant shares that vested immediately (strike $200.93, in the money) = 59.37M. Unvested tranches are tied to future purchases and ignored.

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: Own-history base rate: 2019-2025 median year-end trailing P/E 21.5x x estimated trailing EPS at Oct 2027 of $12.03 = $258.7

inputs_detail.derivation: December close / that year's adjusted EPS, e.g. 2025: 136.37/6.35 = 21.5x; 2022: 100.66/8.61 = 11.7x
At Oct 2027 the trailing four quarters are Q4'26 plus Q1-Q3'27. I approximated this as 0.95 x FY2027 consensus $12.668 = $12.03, since the Q4'26 estimate of $2.55 is below a run-rate 2027 quarter.

bear.story: A 2022/2023-type disappointment. Possible triggers: data-center deliveries slip on the capacity ramp, or a hyperscaler capex pause (Kalshi puts a 2027 recession at 21%). Residential stays soft after a second quiet hurricane season and rate-hike risk (Kalshi March 2027 +25bp ~53%). The tariff-refund tailwind does not repeat. 2027 EPS of about $10.5 at a residential-peer/own-history multiple of about 14x gives about $145. The base rate for this is real: GNRC fell 25% in a day on the Oct 2022 pre-announcement and 24% on the Aug 2023 guidance cut, and 8.8% of its rolling 12-month windows lost more than 40%.

base.story: Consensus broadly delivered. 2027 EPS of about $12.5 comes from $1.35B of 2027-scheduled backlog plus Amazon's $2.4B 2027-28 deliveries, and residential grows mid-single digits. The multiple stays near 20x, between residential and data-center peers, giving about $250 (+11%), close to GNRC's historical median 12-month return of +14.6%.

bull.story: The second hyperscaler agreement is finalised (management: 'at least as big as the first'), Amazon vesting tranches accrue, and capacity triples as planned. The market looks through to 2028 EPS of about $15 at a re-rated 24x, toward data-center peers, giving about $360. This is consistent with the top-quartile historical outcome of about +45% or more.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 14.4x (LII) to 79.1x (BE); trailing EV/EBITDA 10.4x (AOS) to 197.7x (BE). Residential subset fwd P/E median 15.2x; data-center electrical subset 28.6x. EV/EBITDA values are trailing because the source does not show forward figures.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 20.5x 2027 P/E is below the 28.1x peer median and inside the range. GNRC trades at 21.7x forward per StockAnalysis, or 17.8x on 2027 consensus. 15x forward EV/EBITDA is about 20x on a trailing-equivalent basis, below the 26.0x median.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The discount to the median is not a call that GNRC underperforms. It is a mix effect. About half of GNRC's sales and profits come from residential standby generators, a weather- and housing-driven cyclical business whose listed analogues (AOS, LII, ENPH, CMI) trade at 14-17x. Its own long-run year-end trailing P/E median is 14.6x (2013-2025) and 21.5x (2019-2025). The C&I/data-center half justifies a VRT/NVT/POWL-type 28-31x only for that half, and that half is concentrated in two hyperscaler customers. I applied no premium, because nothing shows that GNRC's margins or returns on capital will structurally exceed data-center peers'.

thesis_break_reason: $150 is about 12x 2027 consensus EPS, below the Sept 16, 2026 pre-Amazon-deal close of $175.11 and near the bottom of GNRC's own 2013-2018 P/E range (about 10-15x). At that level the market would be pricing a data-center backlog that is not converting (a delivery slip, cancellation or a hyperscaler capex pause) or a residential downturn severe enough to cut 2027 EPS by 20% or more. Ordinary volatility of 56%/yr gives roughly a 1-in-6 chance of such a move with no news. Below $150 I would assume something fundamental broke, as in the Oct 2022 pre-announcement (-25% in a day), not noise.

Q4/FY2026 results and first FY2027 guidance (EPS consensus $12.67, revenue $6.40B)
FOMC (Kalshi ~53% for a 25bp hike, thin volume). Higher rates are a headwind for residential and housing.
Q1 2027 results: first quarter of Amazon/hyperscaler 2027 deliveries
2027 Atlantic hurricane season and summer grid stress. Outage spikes historically drive home standby demand (EIA: 2024 major-event outage hours were about 2x the decade average).
Q2 2027 results: capacity tripling progress and data-center margin
Definitive agreement and volumes with the second hyperscaler, or added Amazon warrant vesting tranches
Tariff policy: management says further refunds could be offset by higher new tariff levels

key_uncertainties: Conversion of the data-center backlog ($1.35B scheduled for 2027 plus Amazon's $2.4B for 2027-28) against a capacity ramp that has to triple production in about 12 months
Durability of hyperscaler AI capex. Customer concentration is two hyperscalers. Kalshi puts a 2027 recession at 21%.
Residential home standby in a low-outage year after a quiet 2026 hurricane season, plus Fed hike risk in 2027
Quality of 2026 earnings: about $71M of tariff refunds (about 1.5pt of margin) do not recur, and tariff levels may rise
Multiple regime: GNRC has traded from about 10x to 36x trailing in the last decade, and 2021-2022 shows a re-rating can reverse 70% or more within a year
reasoning: Anchor: 148 rolling 12-month windows of GNRC monthly closes (2013-2026) give a median return of +14.6%, mean +26.5%, quartiles -13.5%/+44.6%, 10th/90th percentiles -36%/+119%, and a log sd of 0.50. 8.8% of windows fell more than 40% and 23% rose more than 50%. Current realized vol is 56%. Fundamentals: Q2 2026 EPS of $2.91 beat by about $0.96, but about $71M of pretax tariff refunds (roughly $0.9/share) explain most of the beat, and the stock fell. C&I grew 29% while residential fell 2%. FY2027 consensus EPS has risen from $11.26 to $12.67 in 90 days after the Amazon agreement (warrant for up to 1.69M shares tied to up to $8B of purchases; $2.4B of deliveries expected 2027-28). The valuation blend gives $268. P/E and own-history methods give about $259-260, and EV/EBITDA gives $289. The peer set splits into residential/cyclical (about 15x) and data-center electrical (about 28.6x), and GNRC sits between them. I used three scenarios: bear $145 at 25% (2022/2023-style break; Kalshi 2027 recession 21%; quiet hurricane season), base $250 at 50%, bull $360 at 25%. For the ladder I modeled each scenario as a lognormal (sigma 0.32/0.24/0.26). The mixture has median ~$247, mean ~$259, log sd ~0.42, P(<-40%) ~10.6% and P(>+50%) ~20%. That is close to GNRC's own history and slightly below its realized vol, because 2026 vol was inflated by one-off deal and earnings days. P(>= $225) is 0.59. I shaded the median below the fair value of $268 toward the base-rate median and the generic large-cap drift, because GNRC has a record of guidance resets: Oct 2022 -25% in a day, Aug 2023 -24%, Q3 2025 -17% over 10 days. Limits: I deliberately did not use option-implied data. Forward EV/EBITDA for peers was not available, so I used trailing figures and adjusted them as described. 12 peer comps are mandated for every lane, which pushes the share of in-lane sources below 60%; excluding the comp sources, 9 of 15 sources (60%) are in-lane. Macrotrends was blocked, so I computed the historical P/E myself.
